quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, you should:

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.
Change lanes quickly.
Accelerate quickly.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Slick roads are dangerous. Turns and curves are especially risky. Slow down more on turns in bad weather than you normally would.

questions.question: You are driving and hear a siren behind you. You should:

options.text: Stop where you are.
Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights behind you, slow down and pull safely to the right side of the road. Stop to let the emergency vehicle pass. If you are in heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: You notice the driver ahead is driving with one hand and talking to a passenger. You should:

options.text: Give the vehicle extra space.
Know that the driver is distracted and less safe.
Avoid driving the same way.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving. Avoid talking to passengers, looking for things, reading, or daydreaming. If another driver seems distracted, stay back and give them extra space. Distracted drivers are more likely to crash.

questions.question: Who must wear a safety belt while in a moving vehicle in Oregon?

options.text: The driver and all passengers
Only passengers under the age of 16
Nobody
Only passengers

questions.explanation: Oregon law requires all drivers and passengers to wear safety belts. Properly fastened safety belts protect you best in a crash.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Accelerate to avoid a red light.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Check what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming next. Slow down and stop if you can. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should:

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for help.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit if you miss yours. Do not stop, back up, swerve across lanes, or cross the median on a highway. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Pedestrians ahead.
End of construction zone.
School crossing ahead.
Flagger ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must always be obeyed.
Are merely suggestions.
Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and guide drivers safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know:

options.text: Vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines mark where pedestrians should cross safely. You must stop for any pedestrian in a crosswalk.

questions.question: Before you start the engine, you should:

options.text: Make sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all occupants have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all occupants have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before starting your car, develop the habit of buckling your own seat belt first. Then make sure all passengers buckle theirs.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic signal.
Fire station.
T intersection.
Left turn signal.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you about an upcoming traffic signal. Yellow warning signs have black markings. Be ready to stop for a red light or yellow light, and watch for cross traffic.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is for one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right because of roadwork.
The road ahead turns sharply. Slow down.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply. Slow down.
questions.explanation: This sign means the road ahead has a sharp turn. You should slow down before you reach the curve, just like you would at an intersection.

questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: Loosely.
Snugly across your hip bones and lower belly.
Hidden under the seat.
So the buzzer or light stops working.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly across your hip bones and lower belly.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower belly. The shoulder belt should be comfortable so you can fit your fist between it and your chest.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Pull up next to the driver and yell.
Let it go.
Flash your high beams.
Cut them off in return.

questions.explanation: Do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Avoid road rage by letting it go and continuing to drive safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians walking along the road ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Pedestrians must not cross here.
Watch for construction workers on the road.

questions.explanation: This sign tells you a pedestrian crossing is coming. Drive carefully and watch for people crossing the road.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Open your window.
Stop driving.
Turn on the radio.

questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving under the influence. Stop driving if you feel tired.

questions.question: What should you do to drive safely at night?

options.text: Stay farther behind other cars.
Do not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because you cannot see as well. Take these steps to drive safely when it is dark.

questions.question: When driving on highways, you should:

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to hazards.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready for unexpected hazards. Keep your eyes moving to avoid highway hypnosis. Do not stare at one thing for more than a few seconds.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash?

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Only drive on weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on highways.
Only drive between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing a seat belt is the single best thing you can do to protect yourself from death or injury while driving.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at other cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard flashers. Exit the road carefully and park as far off the road as possible so other drivers can see you. Open your hood to show your car is broken down.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both A and B are true.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B are true.
questions.explanation: Speeding increases the risk of death in a crash. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival is unlikely. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may become impatient and make unsafe moves to pass you.

questions.question: Smoking and preparing to smoke while driving:

options.text: Do not affect driving abilities.
Help maintain driver alertness.
Are distracting activities.
Are not distracting activities.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is a distraction. It takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: Many crashes are caused by:

options.text: Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.
Drivers consistently checking their mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
Drivers maintaining a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers go too fast for road conditions. Always obey speed limits and slow down when conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:

options.text: Can make turning more difficult.
Are likely to hydroplane.
Can increase your stopping distance.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance and make turning harder. Tires with poor tread also increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: You are driving when it starts to sleet or snow. You should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Allow additional distance between your vehicle and the vehicles you are following.
Approach all vehicles with caution.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: In snowy weather, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase your following distance because slippery roads require more distance to stop.

questions.question: If you are driving on the interstate and pass your exit, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn into an exit. If you miss your exit, go to the next one.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.
Speed up to cross the tracks before the gate is lowered.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Not pay attention to how many tracks there are to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop for trains or other vehicles on the tracks.

questions.question: To change lanes you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot in the direction you want to move. Make sure no one else is entering the same lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: You are coming to an intersection and have a green light. Pedestrians are crossing against the red. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians and frighten them so they'll think twice before crossing against a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Stop and let pedestrians cross safely, even if your light is green. Avoid hitting pedestrians under any circumstance.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes:

options.text: Look into the left side mirror.
Look into the right side mirror.
Look into the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: You feel angry after an incident at work. When you get to your car, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly to distract yourself.
Drive fast on the highway to release your anger.
Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving home.
Stop at a bar and have drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving home.
questions.explanation: If you feel upset or angry, wait to calm down before you drive. Driving angry is dangerous. It puts you and other drivers at risk.

questions.question: You can reduce road rage and aggressive driving by:

options.text: Leaving extra time for your trip.
Following posted speed limits.
Using your turn signals correctly.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use your turn signals, follow speed limits, and give yourself extra time. These habits make driving safer and calmer for everyone.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Call the police.
Check if anyone is hurt.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop your car if possible and move it off the road. Check for injuries. Call 911 if anyone is hurt. You must report the crash to police if there is an injury, a death, or more than $1,000 in damage.

questions.question: When driving on wet roads, remember:

options.text: The road is most slippery right when rain starts.
Wet roads can cause your car to hydroplane.
Leave more space to stop.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are dangerous and slippery, especially when rain first starts. Your tires may lose grip on the wet surface. Slow down on wet roads and give yourself extra stopping distance.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Narrow bridge ahead.
A lane is ending or the road is narrowing.
Industrial area ahead.
Highway on-ramp ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane is ending or the road is narrowing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black text on a yellow background. This sign warns you that the right lane is ending or the road is getting narrower ahead.
